adapt_rules.txt:
General SNACS adaptation notes from reviewed guidelines/examples:

1) Motion verb + to + institution/place can take a nonlocative scene role reflecting the semantic type of the landmark, while function remains Goal. Example: "Went to the school" -> role p.Org, function p.Goal.

2) Partitive each/all/some/etc. + of + NP: annotate 'of' with role p.QuantityItem and function p.Whole. Example: "Each of you".

3) Adjective of emotion/evaluation with 'of' marking what the feeling/judgment is about or prompted by may show Stimulus~Topic construal. Example: "proud of your massive contributions" -> role p.Stimulus, function p.Topic.

4) Possessive pronouns/genitives are highly construction-sensitive:
   - If the possessor is an agentive creator/actor relative to a nominalization/event noun, use role p.Agent and function p.Gestalt. Example: "your massive contributions".
   - For ordinary ownership/association with a concrete possessed item, use p.Possessor~p.Possessor. Example: "your money".

5) Temporal span expressions with throughout mark p.Duration~p.Duration. Example: "throughout the year".

6) 'by' with gerund indicating the method used to perform a communicative/action predicate is p.Means~p.Means. Example: "start out by saying".

7) Business names and street names with at/on used literally for location are p.Locus~p.Locus. Examples: "at Lovely Nails", "on Military Road".

Useful caution:
- Do not overgeneralize possessives to p.Possessor; event nominals often license participant roles (Agent, Theme, etc.) with function p.Gestalt per genitive guidelines.
- Role may reflect the scene relation while function reflects the lexical contribution of the adposition/case marker; e.g., destination marker 'to' still contributes Goal even when landmark role is p.Org.
